- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Jagannath Temple is considered one of the holiest shrines in India and is a major pilgrimage destination for Hindus.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The annual Rath Yatra festival is also known as the Chariot Festival and is celebrated in Puri.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] During the Rath Yatra festival, the deities are taken out of the temple and placed on three huge chariots, which are pulled by thousands of devotees through the streets of Puri.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The chariots used in the Rath Yatra are made of wood and decorated with bright colors and flowers.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Rath Yatra festival symbolizes the day when the deities visit their aunt's temple, the Gundicha Temple, which is about 3 km away from the Jagannath Temple.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Rath Yatra festival is a symbol of unity and equality, as people from all castes and creeds participate in the procession.

- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Snana Yatra is a ritual where the deities are bathed with 108 pots of water before the Rath Yatra festival.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Bahuda Yatra is the procession on the ninth day of the Rath Yatra festival when the deities are brought back to the Jagannath Temple.
